confidence.rationale: Restaurant-issued location menus, the Shaw drink menu, catering disclosure, and linked Toast catalog substantiate material scope, extraction, and allergen-evidence discrepancies. Terra's core outcome is correct, although it overextended the Shaw scope to Mount Pleasant drinks, included out-of-scope alcoholic products, and understated valid explicit positive ingredients.

confirmedFindings: The packet identifies 41 affected baseline items: 1:beau-thai-chicken, 2:cauliflower-rice-gf, 3:chicken-cashew-n-s, 4:chicken-satay-n, 5:chumpon-spicy-seafood-rice-gf, 6:congee-with-pork, 7:congee-with-shrimp, 8:crispy-calamari, 9:crispy-roti, 10:crispy-tilapia, 11:crispy-tofu-v-s, 14:fried-banana-v, 18:green-curry-gf, 19:green-salad-n, 20:hot-and-spicy-noodle-bowl-n, 22:kanom-krok, 24:larb-gai-gf, 26:massaman-curry-gf-n, 27:noodle-bowls, 28:noodle-dishesadd-shrimp, 29:omelette, 33:pad-thai-gf-n, 35:papaya-salad-gf-n, 37:pineapple-fried-rice-n, 40:rice-dishesadd-shrimp, 43:shrimp-cakes-s, 44:shrimp-in-garlic-sauce, 46:side-of-green-mango-salad, 47:side-of-sticky-rice, 48:side-of-sweet-sausage, 49:spring-rolls-v, 50:steamed-dumplings-s, 52:stir-fries, 53:street-eggs, 54:thai-donuts, 55:the-hangover-special, 56:tom-kha-soup-gf, 57:tom-yum-soup-gf, 59:vegetable-noodle-bowl-v, 60:wonton-soup-s, and 61:yellow-curry-noodle-bowl-khao-soi.

All 61 baseline records were reconciled exactly once: 4 artifact/not_applicable, 8 variant_match/verified, 9 normalized_match/verified, 15 location_mismatch/accurately_unavailable, and 25 normalized_match/accurately_unavailable. Unique reconciled count is 61 with zero duplicate reconciled keys.
The official pages clearly separate Shaw and Mount Pleasant. Fifteen frozen records sourced only from Mount Pleasant are outside the packet's Shaw location scope.
The official Shaw food page and linked Toast catalog establish a substantial current food inventory. The baseline also contains four non-products: two headings and two add-shrimp modifier lines.

The official Shaw drink page contains a current nonalcoholic catalog, including Thai Tea, Thai Coffee, Coke Products, Sparkling Water, Athletic IPA, and Basil Grapefruit Sparkler. Its omission confirms incomplete current scope and count drift in principle.
Restaurant menu descriptions are incomplete ingredient disclosures. They cannot support allergen negatives, complete allergen arrays, or item-specific mayContain values.

Explicit restaurant-issued positives remain valid narrowly. Examples include egg in Fried Rice and Pad Thai; peanut in Chicken Satay, Green Salad, Papaya Salad, Pad Thai, and Massaman Curry; tree nut from explicitly named cashews; sesame and soy in Crispy Tofu; fish in Crispy Tilapia and Prik Nam Pla; and shellfish in explicitly named shrimp, crab, scallops, squid, or calamari products. Optional shrimp supports only the corresponding configured variant, not every base entrée.
The catering disclosure establishes global kitchen cross-contact context for nuts/seeds, flour, and shellfish. It cannot populate individual mayContain arrays or prove item-specific exposure.

Multi-service, current-only, count-drift, duplicate-presentation, non-exact-reconciliation, cross-contact-review, low-confidence, and scout-risk gates are supported in principle, but the packet's literal two-product abstraction is not a valid complete current-product count.
rejectedFindings: Rejected Terra's inclusion of the Mount Pleasant drink catalog as a missing current product within the verified Shaw scope. It is useful comparison evidence but belongs to a separate location.
Rejected Terra's P4 Toast alcoholic-drinks finding because the governing scout scope requires food and nonalcoholic menu surfaces; alcoholic products are outside that boundary.

Rejected grouping two location-specific drink catalogs into one consolidated P3 product. The Shaw nonalcoholic products require separate enumeration, while Mount Pleasant products must remain outside Shaw reconciliation.
Rejected literal reliance on currentProductCount=2, currentOnlyCount=1, and the consolidated P1/P2 product model. The reopened sources expose many individual current products and presentations.

Rejected the authority_ambiguity gate as framed. Restaurant-issued and restaurant-linked-vendor sources have distinguishable authority tiers; the problem is incomplete allergen evidence, not ambiguous provenance.
Rejected Terra's summary that valid positives are limited to peanuts, sesame, and shellfish. Explicit egg, fish, soy, and cashew/tree-nut positives also remain supportable for exact products.

Rejected converting generic n!/s! markers into a specific allergen when the menu does not identify the nut or seed. Specific mappings require an explicit description such as peanuts, cashews, or sesame.

Rejected culinary-assumption expansion from battered, breaded, wonton, curry, sauce, or similar preparation language to wheat, milk, egg, soy, or other allergens unless the restaurant explicitly names the ingredient or the product identity makes it unavoidable.
Rejected interpreting empty baseline or Terra allergen arrays as evidence of allergen absence or completeness.

additionalEvidence.summary: Official Shaw food menu confirms location scope, current products, dietary-marker limitations, and explicit positives including egg, peanuts, cashews, sesame, soy, fish, and shellfish.
Official Mount Pleasant food menu confirms that the fifteen location-mismatched baseline records belong to a separately labeled location.
Official Shaw drink menu exposes a current nonalcoholic catalog omitted from the frozen baseline and Terra's complete enumeration.
Official catering page states that the kitchens use nuts/seeds, flour, and shellfish and that cross-contamination can occur; this is global context rather than item-level may-contain evidence.
Linked Shaw ordering catalog confirms numerous current food and nonalcoholic products and explicit named ingredients, but its authority must remain restaurant-linked-vendor.

summary: The effective outcome remains discrepancy_found. The 41 affected baseline items sit within a complete 61-record reconciliation containing 15 wrong-location records and four extraction artifacts. Current Shaw nonalcoholic products were missed, allergen evidence is incomplete, and literal deterministic product counts are unreliable. Terra correctly rejected negatives, complete arrays, and item-level cross-contact conclusions, but overreached into Mount Pleasant and alcoholic-drink scope and failed to preserve all valid explicit positives.
coordinatorActions: Return the adjudication as discrepancy_found and do not mark codex_verified.
Re-enumerate individual current Shaw food and nonalcoholic products; exclude Mount Pleasant and alcoholic products from the Shaw catalog boundary.
Remove headings and modifier text from standalone product records and rerun deterministic counts afterward.
Preserve narrow explicit positives for exact products and configured variants while keeping all unestablished allergens unavailable.
Do not derive specific allergens solely from generic n!/s! markers or culinary assumptions.
Keep the catering cross-contact statement as global restaurant context and do not populate item-level mayContain arrays from it.
Retain source authority distinctions between restaurant-issued pages and the linked Toast vendor.
